gen-gf-grandstander-gf-lexend-tera: Grandstander's lines hold one width and stay open, never curling shut. Lexend Tera sets its sans letters far apart like stepping stones, so give it a modest size and the single-weight strokes have space to breathe.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-syriac-: Noto Sans Syriac Eastern is approachable, with tall lowercase and curve endings that keep their distance. Grandstander above it draws flat, unmodulated strokes with a bold, expressive streak, so the two feel like a loud voice and a friendly one.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-strait: Strait is a plain sans with big round lowercase bowls, friendly from the first word. Under Grandstander's drafting-pen outlines, a long passage would feel soft and rounded, easy to settle into line after line.
gen-gf-grandstander-instrument-sans: Grandstander brings bold, expressive lettering with short ascenders and a tall x-height, drawn with one constant nib width. And Instrument Sans follows with open-ended c shapes and a stroke that never varies, so a long passage would read smooth and modern.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-karma: Distinctive from the first glance, Gugi has no hairlines anywhere, while Karma's serif joins taper modestly without vanishing. The pairing's strongest quality is trust wrapped in swagger.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-quicksand: Quicksand reads like blown glass bulbs, with tall lowercase bowls and bars of identical thickness across the line. Under Gugi's bold heading, a longer passage would feel gentle and approachable.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-ranade: Ranade spreads its sans letters wide, with stroke ends set far apart. Next to Gugi's neon-tube consistency, its subtly shifting weight is the pair's strongest quality, a bold heading meeting an organic, professional body.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-cascadia-code: Cascadia Code reads as widely spaced, wire-like monoline type with smooth bends. Gugi's tall lowercase and open terminals make a bold front, and that spacious body is where the pair's strongest quality lives.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-lexend-zetta: Gugi's lowercase nearly reaches its capitals, with terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. Lexend Zetta follows in widely tracked ribbon-like strokes, so the bold heading and the tall-bodied sans-serif text sit together with plenty of space.
gen-gf-halant-general-sans: Halant offers refined, literary joins that thin gently without turning spindly, with spacious gaps at its curve terminals. And General Sans does the opposite job best, keeping unshaded, constant strokes and a tall x-height that fills the line.
